STEP 1 - Vessel type: Square flat plate. It has a rim band and a flat centre with no inner wall, and the food sits on the surface.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Square plates are typically 20-30 cm. This one looks medium, so I take about 24 cm.
b) Reference: a cherry tomato (3 cm) appears about 40 px across, and the plate spans about 455 px. That gives about 34 cm, but the overhead angle and perspective inflate it. I trust the type estimate more, so width is about 24 cm and area is about 576 cm².

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Salad greens (romaine and leaves): covers about 35% of the plate, roughly 200 cm². Average thickness about 1.5 cm, so volume about 300 ml. Raw leafy greens at 0.15 g/ml gives about 45-60 g. Use 60 g.
- Cherry tomatoes: 2 visible, so 2 × 15 g = 30 g.
- Dark pieces (olives or similar): about 3 pieces at 4 g each = 12 g.
- Pizza or flatbread slice with tomato sauce and cheese: footprint about 6 × 4 cm = 24 cm², thickness about 1.5 cm, so about 36 ml. At density 1.0 g/ml, use 40 g.
- Dressing (Caesar-style, visible on the greens): about 10 g.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: No clear base layer beyond the greens. The plate is lightly loaded, so no large hidden mass.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Romaine/raw greens: 17
- Cherry tomato: 18
- Olives: 115
- Pizza slice: 250
- Creamy dressing: 470

Totals: greens 10 kcal, tomato 5 kcal, olives 14 kcal, pizza 100 kcal, dressing 47 kcal. Total about 176 kcal and about 150 g.
